title: MegaScale-Infer: Serving Mixture-of-Experts at Scale with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism
technique: Disaggregate attention and FFN/expert modules onto separate GPUs with independent parallelism; ping-pong pipeline parallelism over micro-batches; custom M2N communication library; heterogeneous GPU deployment plan search

optimized_metrics.evidence: we focus on maximizing the cost-normalized decoding throughput, subject to a specified time-between-tokens (TBT) latency constraint. Specifically, for homogeneous deployment, we use per-GPU decoding throughput
Our goal is to identify the deployment plan that maximizes throughput per unit cost (e.g., dollar).
Following prior work [82], we set the TBT requirement to 150 milliseconds.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we set the TBT requirement to 150 milliseconds

optimized_metrics.evidence: this pipeline should be meticulously co-designed with the model parallelism strategies of each module to maximize GPU utilization while adhering to latency requirements.

headline_claim.text: MegaScale-Infer achieves up to 1.90× higher per-GPU throughput than state-of-the-art solutions.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 8(a),(c), 9(a): per-GPU / per-cost decoding and end-to-end throughput
Fig 9 throughput per cost (normalized purchase price, Table 3)
Figs 11-12 M2N median and P99 latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: for homogeneous deployment, we use per-GPU decoding throughput, i.e., tokens generated per second, excluding the first output token, divided by the number of GPUs, as the primary metric. For heterogeneous deployment, we report per-cost decoding throughput.
metric_definitions.notes: Output tokens only, excludes first token and prefill; decode-phase only; normalized per GPU or per cost.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Here we define cost with the normalized purchase price as shown in Table 3, which can easily be replaced by the rental price for cloud service
when measuring decoding throughput and time between tokens, we exclude the prefill phase and consider only the iteration time and output tokens of the decoding phase.
metric_definitions.notes: TBT = decode iteration time; reported as mean (also median/tail in M2N micro-benchmarks).

slo_spec: Single TBT requirement of 150 ms per token (following prior work) applied as constraint Titer <= SLO in deployment plan search; max global batch size found by binary search under it
load_regime: Fixed (searched) global decode batch size per system under 150 ms TBT cap; prefill and decode temporally separated, decode-only measurement; synthetic/production-like in-house workload (median sequence length given)
tradeoff_acknowledged: Disaggregation adds per-layer communication and does not reduce individual per-token latency; mean TBT is comparable to baselines (sometimes slightly higher), the gain is throughput at the same TBT bound.
hardware: Homogeneous NVIDIA Ampere-class cluster (NVLink); heterogeneous H20 (attention) + L40S (experts)
extractor_notes: Latency is a constraint, not an objective. The text of §4.2 says 'minimize the throughput per unit cost' but the evident intent (and Alg. 1: plan*.tpuc < plan.tpuc updates) is maximizing throughput per unit cost. Throughput excludes the first output token and prefill. M2N communication library reports median and P99 latency, but only for the micro-benchmark (not request-level). Reports 1.5-2.0x serving cost reduction in production.

tail_audit.metrics: M2N communication P99 latency and median (reported); TBT constraint 150 ms (no percentile)
